column1: # MITRE ATT&CK and ATLAS references, and NIST CSF 2.0 outcomes, for each kind of finding the fleet result
# names, shown by gird-report.ps1. One line each, tab separated. After editing, run: bash tools/gen.sh
# The mapping is Blindspot's own, not MITRE's or NIST's. Blindspot reads files: it never detects a technique in use.
# A line goes in only when the result line itself carries enough to know the technique applies to that
# finding on that system. Where it does not, the word gets a none line saying why.
#   word       a finding word of the fleet inventory value, as gird-report.ps1's $Items lists it. Every
#              word has at least one attack, one atlas and one csf line, mapped or none (gen.sh refuses a word
#              without one, and a word gird-report.ps1 does not know)
#   os         all, mac or win: the line applies only to results from that system (a Windows result
#   scope      all, or the incident ids (data/incidents.tsv) the line applies to, comma separated: only
#              for a word whose value lists incident ids (incidents, lockfile, update, remove). The report
#              shows such a line only for PCs whose result names one of them
#   framework  attack, atlas or csf (NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0)
#   id         the technique id or the CSF Subcategory id, or - on a none line
#   name       the technique's name as MITRE's page gives it (a sub-technique as parent: name), or the
#              Subcategory's outcome as NIST's text gives it, or -
#   tactics    the tactics MITRE lists for the technique, comma separated; for csf the Function, then the
#              Category (Identify, Protect or Detect only; gen.sh knows each Category used, by name); or -
#   relation   exposure: Blindspot found something the technique could exploit
#              indicator: a trace that a published incident links to the technique
#              supports (csf only): the finding helps an organization work toward the outcome on that
#              computer. Never a statement that the outcome is met or missed
#              none: no technique or outcome fits; the note says why
#   note       on a none line, why no technique fits, as the report shows it; - otherwise
# CSF ids, Function and Category names and outcome text are from NIST CSWP 29, The NIST Cybersecurity
# Framework (CSF) 2.0, 26 February 2024, Appendix A (https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.CSWP.29), read on
# 18 November 2026. No finding kind shows that an outcome is not achieved: each Protect outcome depends on
# what the organization authorized or decided, which Blindspot cannot see. So every csf line is supports.
#   ID.RA-01: a weakness Blindspot identifies and records (a readable key, an SSH key with no passphrase,
#   a link to authorized_keys, an agent set to run without asking, a tool with a published fix).
#   DE.CM-09: reading software and files for published malware traces; the leads fit "potentially".
#   PR.PS-02: software to update or to remove.
#   Tested and not used: ID.AM-02, ID.AM-04, ID.RA-03, PR.AA-01, PR.AA-05, PR.DS-01, PR.PS-01, PR.PS-05
#   and all of DE.AE (Blindspot does not analyze or correlate events).
# Read on 18 November 2026: ATT&CK Enterprise v20.1 (https://attack.mitre.org/resources/versions/, current
# since 13 October 2026), each technique's page; ATLAS release 2026.10 of 28 October 2026, from the data the
#   wiper: T1543.001 Launch Agent. A Mac's wiper finding is any one of the wiper's files (data/indicators.tsv:
#   its launch agent, its systemd service, its shell script or its config folder), and the result does not
#   say which, so it does not show a launch agent was found. Also T1543.002 Systemd Service (Linux only,
#   and the fleet result comes from macOS and Windows) and T1053.005 Scheduled Task (what Blindspot finds
#   on Windows is a folder, not a scheduled task).
#   wiper: T1485 is an indicator, not a sign the wiper is set to run: for the same reason, the file found
#   may be a script or a folder that nothing starts.
#   incidents: T1543.001 and T1543.002 for an incident's startup file (the result does not say which file
#   planted: AML.T0010.001, which fits only lightning's payload; the result gives a count, not the incident.
#   sessions: AML.T0085.002 Data from AI Services: Conversation Context and Memory, which is about getting
#   an AI service to reveal what it holds. What Blindspot finds is a key in a file on disk: AML.T0055.
#   on-open: T1195.001 (its text names IDE task files and coding agent configuration files) is about
#   such a file reaching a person in a compromised project or tool. The count also takes in a person's own
#   settings, and Blindspot cannot tell one that came in a cloned project from one the person wrote.
#   on-open: AML.T0081 Modify AI Agent Configuration. The count also takes in editor tasks that run when
#   a folder opens (gird-check.sh, folderOpen tasks), which are editor settings, not an agent's, and the
#   ssh-links on Windows: T1098.004 lists ESXi, IaaS, Linux, network devices and macOS as its platforms.
# T1698 Indirect Prompt Injection lists SaaS and Windows as its platforms, so it is for Windows results only.
# AML.T0055 lists Credential Access as its only tactic in ATLAS 2026.10.
# AML.T0010.001 names T1195.002 as its ATT&CK counterpart; ATT&CK itself places npm and Python packages
# under T1195.001, which these lines follow.
